**Claim** — PM loop `domain:cli`, session `session_0158ZQo7LiHSxGWpYKuPq1wu` (os-help seat, #6024), wave 5 (backfilling the slot #7450 freed).

**Prioritised as the most destructive card in the queue.** It carries no `security` label, but a single authorized API call takes platform functionality out of a live deployment with no recovery short of a restart. That outranks the rest of the current queue on blast radius.

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7560-package-lifecycle-readonly-gate`
- **Scope**: `PATCH /packages/:id/disable` and `DELETE /packages/:id` must refuse a **platform** package with the ADR-0070 read-only refusal, in the same shape other protected-resource writes use. ⛔ Do not invent a new refusal vocabulary — find how ADR-0070 is already enforced elsewhere and match it.
- **The card's own distinction is load-bearing and must not be collapsed**: #7033 / PR #7083 added *caller* authorization to the whole `/packages` domain (writes need `manage_metadata`, reads the D4 set, plus an anonymous gate). That is **who may call**. This card is **what the route may do once the caller is allowed** — an authorized admin can still disable and delete a platform package. Neither a duplicate nor a regression of #7033; it is a second, missing check on the same routes. ⛔ Do not "fix" it by tightening the caller gate.
- **File surface (expected)**: `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (per #7033's census) and/or `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` + tests.
- ⛔ **Serial constraints — three cards are live on `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`** (#7523 reports-delete, #7525 error mapping, #7526 `/meta` mounting). Your surface should not be that file at all; if you find the lifecycle routes are wired there, **report back before editing** rather than colliding.
- ⚠️ **Related but separate, ⛔ not yours**: #7563 (the REST package registrar not mounted on showcase, so `POST /packages/publish` is absorbed by `/packages/:id`). Same route family, different defect — leave it.
- **Accept bar**: both operations refused for a platform package **and** still working for a non-platform one — a fix that refuses everything is not a fix. Prove the tests can fail.
- **Tier / container**: M · `claude-opus-5` · `mode:cloud`.

**os-dev-report** — #7560 · branch `claude/issue-7560-package-lifecycle-readonly-gate` · draft PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#7599

## Status: `done`

## Root cause

`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` — the `/packages` domain dispatcher body, exactly where #7033's census put it. The two lifecycle routes ran their mutation unconditionally once the caller cleared `requireManageMetadata`:

- `PATCH /:id/disable` → `registry.disablePackage(id)` then `setPackageDisabled(...)`
- `DELETE /:id` → `registry.uninstallPackage(id)` then `protocol.deletePackage(...)`

Neither consulted ADR-0070's read-only rule. That rule *existed* — as a **private** method `isWritablePackage` on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:8305`), reachable only from the metadata authoring path. So `saveMetaItem` refused to author one field *into* a platform package while `DELETE` removed the whole package from the running deployment.

**⛔ `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` is NOT in the diff** — the lifecycle routes are not wired there. No collision with #7523 / #7525 / #7526.

## One correction to the card's blast radius

The card says the packages come back after a restart. True for **`DELETE`**. **Not true for `disable`**: `setPackageDisabled` (`packages/runtime/src/package-state-store.ts:70`) persists to `<OS_HOME>/package-state/<env>.json`, and `SchemaRegistry` replays it at boot through `initialDisabledPackageIds` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:2202`). **A disabled platform package stayed disabled across restarts** — the disable half was the more durable of the two defects, not the lesser one. The card's "no way back short of a restart" understates it: for `disable`, a restart was not a way back either.

## The distinction, held

The caller gate is **byte-untouched**. In every new test the caller holds `manage_metadata` and is refused anyway. The new gate is deliberately **not** caller-sensitive — no `isSystem` bypass, unlike `requireManageMetadata` — because read-only is a property of the *package*. Pinned directly: *"is NOT the #7033 caller gate: the admin is authorized (no 401/403) and still refused"*.

## Precedent found — no new vocabulary invented

ADR-0070 is already enforced on the authoring axis, and this reuses it verbatim:

| | Existing (authoring) | New (lifecycle) |
|---|---|---|
| predicate | `isWritablePackage` (private, protocol.ts) | **same function**, now exported |
| status | `422` | `422` |
| code | `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` | `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` |
| details | `packageId`, `docs: docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md` | same |

The predicate moved to `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts` and is exported; `protocol.ts` now delegates to it. Both callers **reference** one definition — a second hand-kept copy is precisely the drift that produced this defect. Ledger: `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` registered as a second **emitter** under `@objectstack/runtime` (the ledger header explicitly provides for this: "listed once per emitting package — provenance, not identity").

Both read-only signals covered: booted **code** package (`engine.manifests` — the repro's "code-loaded") and **platform-delivered** manifest `scope` ∈ {`system`, `cloud`}.

## Accept bar

| Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| disable refused for platform pkg | 3 cases (system / cloud / code-loaded), `enabled` still `true`, `status` not `disabled` |
| DELETE refused for platform pkg | 3 cases, **`registry.getAllPackages()` unchanged** |
| **the card's observable** | listing asserted, not the status code — tests drive a **real `SchemaRegistry`**, not `vi.fn()` doubles |
| still works for non-platform | writable pkg disables (listing shows `disabled`), re-enables, and deletes (leaves listing); read-only siblings untouched |
| not an existence oracle | unknown id still `404`, not `422` |

## Mutation table — every new test proven able to fail

Applied to the merged tree, suite run (`packages-readonly-gate` + pre-existing `packages-capability-gate`, 91 tests), reverted. *Predicate mutations needed a `metadata-protocol` rebuild — `@objectstack/runtime` resolves the built `dist`, so the first pass of those four was a silent no-op and was re-run.*

| # | Mutation | Result | Red |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `DELETE` gate removed (pre-fix) | 6 / 85 | 3 DELETE cases, isSystem, envelope, verb |
| M2 | `disable` gate removed (pre-fix) | 5 / 86 | 3 disable cases, axis, verb |
| M3 | predicate always `false` — **outage shape** | 8 / 83 | writable disable+delete, both 404s, **+4 pre-existing #7033 tests** |
| M4 | code-loaded signal dropped | 2 / 89 | both code-loaded cases only |
| M5 | manifest-`scope` signal dropped | 8 / 83 | both system + both cloud, isSystem, axis, envelope, verb |
| M6 | `DELETE` gate moved **after** `uninstallPackage` | 6 / 85 | the **listing** assertions — delete-first-refuse-second |
| M7 | `disable` gate moved **after** `disablePackage` | 3 / 88 | the `enabled`/`status` assertions |
| M8 | refusal restated as `PACKAGE_READ_ONLY` | 7 / 84 | 6 refusal cases + envelope shape |
| M9 | unknown id treated as read-only | 2 / 89 | both 404 cases only |
| M10 | blanket caller bypass re-added | 10 / 81 | 6 refusal cases, isSystem, axis, envelope, verb |

M6 is the one that matters for the card's instruction: it keeps the **422** and still fails, because the package left the listing. Status-only assertions would have passed it. M3 is the accept-bar one: refusing everything breaks four of #7033's own allow-path tests too.

## Files

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts` **(new)** — exported `isWritablePackage`
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` — private method delegates
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` — export
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` — `requireWritablePackage` + both call sites
- `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` — second emitter registered
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-readonly-gate.test.ts` **(new, 15 tests)**
- `.changeset/packages-lifecycle-readonly-gate.md`

## Gates

`pnpm lint` ✓ · `pnpm typecheck` ✓ (spec, runtime; `metadata-protocol` has no `typecheck` script) · runtime **2005** ✓ · spec **9805** ✓ · metadata-protocol **1051** ✓ · objectql **3153** ✓ · rest **1344** ✓ · changeset ✓ · no `content/docs/releases/**` edits ✓

## #7563 — neither helped nor hindered

This adds a gate **inside** an already-reached handler; it touches no mounting, no registrar, no route matching. #7563's fix (mounting the REST package registrar so `POST /packages/publish` stops being absorbed by `/packages/:id`) is orthogonal. One note for whoever takes it: if that mount lands, `/packages/publish` will parse as `parts.length === 1` here too — worth confirming the literal `publish` segment can't reach `DELETE`/`PATCH` handling for a package named `publish`.

## Follow-up worth a card (deliberately NOT done — out of scope)

`PATCH /packages/:id` (manifest edit: name / description / version) mutates a **platform package's manifest** with the same absent gate — `registry.updatePackageManifest` rewrites the shipped manifest in the running registry. Not fixed here because this card scopes to disable + delete, and I'd rather the PM decide than widen a destructive-path PR. The fix is one line: the same `requireWritablePackage(deps, qlService, id, 'edit')` call. `POST /:id/publish-drafts`, `/discard-drafts`, `/rollback` and `/adopt-orphans` are arguably the same family and deserve a look under one card rather than piecemeal.

**ACCEPT** — PR #7599, head `5a75743f5`.

**The dev corrected this card's blast-radius claim with a measurement, and the correction makes the defect worse than filed.** The card said the packages come back after a restart. That is true for `DELETE` — they are code-loaded — but **not for `disable`**: `setPackageDisabled` persists the choice to `<OS_HOME>/package-state/<env>.json`, which `SchemaRegistry` replays at boot, so a disabled platform package **stayed disabled across restarts**. The "confined to the running deployment, recoverable by restart" framing — which I repeated in the claim comment — was only half right, and the half that was wrong is the persistent half. Recorded here so the card's own history does not preserve the understatement.

- **The two-axis distinction held.** #7033 / PR #7083 gave the domain *caller* authorization (who may call); this is the second check on the same routes (what the route may do once the caller is allowed). **The caller gate is untouched** — verified by diff. ⛔ It was not "fixed" by tightening #7083, which was the failure mode I flagged.
- **No new vocabulary**, as required: the refusal is ADR-0070's existing **422 / `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`** — the same code `saveMetaItem` already throws when asked to author *into* a read-only package. The dev found the precedent rather than inventing a shape.
- **One definition instead of two that drift.** The predicate moved out of `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`'s private method into `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s exported `isWritablePackage(engine, id)`, now referenced by both callers. That is the #7270 lesson applied unprompted — a rule spelled twice is a rule that will diverge. Both signals covered: a booted code package (`engine.manifests`) and a `system`/`cloud` manifest scope.
- **Deliberately not caller-sensitive**, with a stated reason: no `isSystem` bypass, unlike the write gate, because read-only is a property of **the package**, not of who is asking. Internal teardown calls `registry.uninstallPackage` directly and never passes through a gate, so nothing legitimate is broken.
- **The accept bar was met on the observable, not the status code**: the new suite drives a **real** `SchemaRegistry` and asserts the registry **listing** in both directions — packages an org owns still disable, re-enable and delete exactly as before. A status-code-only assertion would not have caught the original harm, which was the package vanishing from the listing.
- **Region discipline**: `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` untouched — verified by diff, so #7525 / #7526 / #7486 are unaffected.
- **CI, conclusions read personally**: ESLint `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Check Changeset `success`, Spec property liveness `success`, all Test Core / Dogfood / Temporal shards `success` — 26 checks, zero failures.
